lemmas.statement: Replaying the first-separation history from the empty regime yields the first-separation regime.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: example : GenesisComputation.GenesisCopy.replayE GenesisComputation.firstSeparationHistory GenesisComputation.emptyRegime = some GenesisComputation.firstSeparationRegime := GenesisComputation.first_separation_replay

lemmas.statement: The resulting regime tells datum 0 and datum 1 apart by a unary instance.

near_misses.claim: A single admitted datum already yields an alphabet of two marks.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Separation needs two distinct data, so with one datum there is no pair to separate.

near_misses.claim: Demand (0,1) is satisfied without any instance on datum 0.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: UnarySep needs an instance that distinguishes the data, so an empty instance list cannot separate them.

open_obligations: Exact signatures of firstSeparationHistory, firstSeparationRegime and first_separation_replay are not shown, so the Lean skeletons are unelaborated.
